title: Robinhood Ventures Fund II invests in Opalite Health
summary: Robinhood Ventures Fund II backed Opalite Health in August 2026, supporting faster expansion of AI medical interpretation across health systems.
body_text: Robinhood Ventures Fund II just listed on the NYSE to give everyday investors access to private-market companies before an IPO. One of those companies is us. If you're curious what that means for your patients, your team, or your contract with us, this is a quick read. Opalite Health joins the Robinhood Ventures Fund II portfolio Robinhood Ventures Fund II (NYSE: RVII) has invested in Opalite Health. We are now part of the RVII portfolio, and we are glad to share the news with the clinicians, administrators, and health systems who work with us. The pairing makes sense once you look at what each side is trying to do. Our work starts from a simple belief: language should never stand between a patient and the care they need. RVII operates from a parallel conviction in a different arena, that access to venture capital and the wealth it can create should not be reserved for a narrow few. Both missions come down to the same thing. They widen the door for people who have historically been kept outside it. For us, that means giving patients with limited English proficiency a way to understand and be understood during a medical encounter. For RVII, it means opening private-market investing to a far broader base. The investment brings those two efforts into the same room. What Robinhood Ventures Fund II is Robinhood Ventures Fund II is a closed-end Business Development Company , or BDC, governed under the Investment Company Act of 1940. It is managed by Robinhood Ventures, an SEC-registered investment adviser and a subsidiary of Robinhood Markets. The structure is what makes it interesting for everyday investors. Instead of waiting for a startup to go public, retail investors can buy shares in a diversified portfolio of private companies through a single NYSE listing. The ticker is RVII on Robinhood . The IPO is expected on August 13, 2026, priced at $25.00 per share, with the share request window open through August 12, 2026. At IPO, the fund is set to hold roughly 80 private companies. Here is how the fund's fees and disclosures are structured: [@portabletext/react] Unknown block type "table", specify a component for it in the `components.types` prop "Retail investors no longer have to wait until a company's IPO to be part of an early growth journey." Sarah Pinto, Head of Robinhood Ventures Inside the portfolio The fund's thesis is narrow by design. RVII invests primarily in Y Combinator-backed companies and businesses founded by YC alumni. Opalite Health is a Y Combinator-backed company from the W26 batch, so we fit squarely within that mandate. As of the July 15, 2026 snapshot, the fund's holdings broke down across sectors like this: [@portabletext/react] Unknown block type "table", specify a component for it in the `components.types` prop Opalite Health on Robinhood sits inside that Healthcare allocation at a 1.12% position. That is roughly in line with how the fund is built, since most holdings land near 1% of the fund each. No single company dominates, which is the point of a diversified BDC. It also means our slice of the portfolio reflects a deliberate bet on healthcare access, not a passing interest. Why language access in healthcare Consider a patient who describes chest pain through a family member doing the translating. Details get softened. A medication name gets garbled. The wrong prescription goes home, and the patient returns sicker than before. For patients with limited English proficiency , that scenario is not rare. Language gaps contribute to delayed diagnoses, medication errors , weak informed consent, and worse outcomes. Opalite was built for that gap. The suite covers real-time AI medical interpretation across more than 150 languages and dialects, multilingual AI scribing, and medical document translation. It is purpose-built for clinical settings, trained on millions of minutes of real clinical conversations. It is HIPAA compliant and integrated with Epic, Cerner, and other major EHRs. The accuracy question matters most here. In an independent study conducted with Johns Hopkins Medicine, Opalite produced more than 90% fewer major and critical errors compared with certified medical interpreters ( validation study ). The founders Cathleen Kuo, MD, our co-founder and CEO, is a physician. When she was 16, her mother was placed on the wrong medication after her symptoms were mistranslated, then returned to the hospital. That failure shaped why she built Opalite. Alexander Mehregan, co-founder and CTO, previously worked at Apple on Apple Intelligence and the next generation of Siri. He leads product engineering and AI infrastructure. What changes for Opalite Health customers The short answer is nothing. Opalite remains an independent company, and the tools you rely on every day stay exactly where they are. Your EHR integrations and every service commitment in your contract carry on unchanged. This investment does not alter who runs Opalite or how we support you. What it does is add a backer. Robinhood Ventures now joins our existing investors, including Y Combinator, which supported us through the W26 batch. The practical benefit shows up in our roadmap. With more capital behind us, we can move faster on the work customers ask for most: Expanding language coverage for patients with limited English proficiency Deepening integrations with Epic, Cerner, and other systems Scaling to more health systems that need reliable language access There is also a public dimension to this. As of August 13, 2026, anyone who believes a patient should be understood by their care team can own a piece of that mission through RVII. The fine print A quick word on what this post is and is not. This is a company announcement. It is not investment advice, and it is not an offer to sell securities. Opalite Health is not selling shares to the public. RVII is a fund managed by Robinhood Ventures that holds a stake in Opalite as part of a portfolio of roughly 80 companies total. Early-stage investing carries risk. Before requesting shares, review the fund's prospectus and risk disclosures on robinhood.com. Thank you to the Robinhood Ventures team. To our customers and patients: this is for you. Final thoughts on Opalite Health joining the RVII portfolio The investment does not change what you rely on day to day, but it does change how fast we can move on the things you ask for most. Better language coverage, deeper EHR integrations, and more health systems served are all on the roadmap. Book a demo to see how Opalite fits your clinical workflows and language-access program.

title: Don't Settle for Less When it Comes to Deposit Insurance
summary: Standard FDIC insurance covers $250,000 per depositor. Here is how sweep networks raise that ceiling.
body_text: When it comes to banking, don't lose the plot With all the perks and tools that modern bank accounts offer, it’s easy to forget about one of the main reasons banks were created more than a thousand years ago: to keep your money safe. Back then, “safety” looked like stone walls and well-made padlocks. Today, it comes in the form of FDIC insurance. 4,278 financial institutions are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), which includes the vast majority of banks in the United States. Founded in the midst of the Great Depression, the FDIC was created to protect consumers from losing their money in the case of a bank failure. If you’re FDIC insured up to a certain amount, those funds don’t disappear if and when a bank does. People and businesses alike often overlook details about FDIC insurance because they don’t think a bank failure would ever impact them. The reality couldn’t be more distant. There have been 574 bank failures in the United States since 2000, with an average of 22 a year. In 2010 alone, 157 banks failed and over $96 billion in consumer funds were put at risk. Just about every dollar that wasn’t FDIC insured evaporated into thin air. While most everyday customers were able to recoup their losses, plenty of businesses and corporations took bigger hits from these collapses. That’s because the limit for FDIC insurance is $250,000 per depositor, per bank. This is perfectly suitable for the average Joe, but it may not be nearly enough for companies and well-funded startups. So far in 2026, the median series A funding round raised $15 million, while the mean was $24.5 million. While most of those funds will be reinvested back into those startups, shrewd founders will often set some aside in a high-yield savings account to earn idle cash while it’s not in use. That money isn’t fully safe. If you set $5 million aside and the bank holding it fails, you’ll only get $250,000 back with standard FDIC insurance. At that point, $250k might feel like chump change. So what’s the solution? Do American companies walk around all day with millions of dollars exposed to the elements? Not all do. Some use sweep networks. The standard in finance Slash goes above with better controls, better rewards, and better support for your business. Get Started What’s a sweep network? Sweep networks can multiply the FDIC’s $250,000 limit by spreading deposits across separate accounts held at interconnected partner banks.² The process is automatic; if your account surpasses $250k, a system “sweeps” the excess amounts into a partner bank account to make sure it’s insured under that account’s ceiling. From your point of view, the main account balance doesn’t actually change, but a partner bank is responsible for protecting a certain chunk of the overall total. If you have $2 million in your main account, this process would take place across seven partner banks. Holding $400,000 in a standard FDIC-insured bank account is kind of like bringing your luggage to the airport and handing it to Bag Check with a pile of clothes sitting on top of it. Just bring a second suitcase. In the same way you would bring multiple suitcases to protect your clothes, you should use multiple partner bank accounts to protect your money. How high can this protection get? Well, while an airport won’t let you bring dozens of suitcases, sweep networks will often let you use dozens of partner accounts. Column N.A., for example, allows users to spread their deposits across up to 800 partner banks through an arrangement with IntraFi’s sweep network, meaning balances can be insured up to $150 million dollars. This goes far beyond many other banks that utilize sweep networks, such as SoFi and JP Morgan ($3 million max each). $150 million in FDIC insurance with Slash While a few million is a better ceiling than $250k, some companies need far more protection: venture-backed startups after a funding round, multi-national corporations with ten figure 10Ks. You can’t bank directly with Column N.A., as they’re an API-first partner bank for developers and fintech companies. If you want to access hundreds of millions in insurance, try opening a business checking account with Slash.¹ Through a partnership with Column, Slash users can keep balances of more than $150 million insured, meaning large funding rounds don’t have to come with unnecessary risk. Slash also offers a Treasury account backed by money market investments from BlackRock and Morgan Stanley, which can earn users up to 3.84% annualized yield.⁶ These balances come with Securities Investor Protection Corporation (SIPC) protection up to $500,000, which is currently the maximum amount. Whether you have $1,000 or $100,000,000, your funds are FDIC insured in a Slash business account, with banking services provided by Column N.A., Member FDIC. title: What Is an Agentic Design System? A Practical Definition
summary: What is an agentic design system? A practical definition, the four stages from documented to agentic, and how to tell which one your team is on.
body_text: Four stages, and how to work out which one you're on. An agentic design system is one that AI agents can query, resolve and act on, rather than only read. It exposes tokens, components and rules as structured data an agent can retrieve on demand, and it lets agents contribute changes back rather than only consuming. The word doing the work is act . A documented design system tells an agent what you decided. An agentic one lets the agent resolve that decision to a concrete value, apply it, and in some cases propose a change to it. Key Takeaway : An agentic design system is not a design system with AI features attached. It's a design system that agents can query for specific answers and act on. Most teams are two stages away from one, and the gap is structural rather than technological. How is it different from an AI-ready design system? AI-ready describes preparation. Agentic describes participation. An AI-ready design system is structured well enough that an agent can consume it: consistent naming, clean token architecture, documented component APIs. That work is necessary and most teams should do it first. An agentic design system adds two things on top. Agents can retrieve exactly the slice they need rather than being handed everything. And agents can write back, opening pull requests, updating documentation, flagging drift. Jan Six , who works on design systems at GitHub, put the underlying problem well in his talk at the AI Design Systems Conference : "The invisible part of your system is way bigger than your visible part. If the agent can't see it, it has to hallucinate." Making the invisible part visible is AI-readiness. Letting agents work with it is agentic. The four stages Most teams recognise themselves somewhere on this ladder. Stage 1: Documented. The system exists and is written down for people. Guidelines, usage rules, examples, all in prose. An agent pointed at it can read the words and infer, which produces output that looks right and often isn't. Stage 2: Machine-readable. Tokens have resolvable values. Components have documented props, variants and states in a structured format. The information stops being paragraphs and starts being data. Diana Wolosin , a senior design system designer at Indeed, ran a benchmark that puts numbers on this stage. Testing 1,056 prompts across eight configurations, Markdown documentation consumed roughly 30,000 tokens per query and reached 82% coverage with hallucinations. Structured JSON reached higher accuracy using 80% fewer tokens, at roughly a fifth of the annual cost. Her framing of why: "JSON is like a contract. It has explicit keys, explicit values, explicit boundaries, and there is no ambiguity." Stage 3: Queryable. The structured data is served, usually over MCP, so an agent asks for what it needs at the moment it needs it. This is where scoping starts to matter. An agent handed the entire system performs worse than one handed the relevant part, and every unnecessary token in the window is one not spent on the task. Stage 4: Agentic. Agents both read and write. They propose token changes, draft documentation, open issues when they find drift, and run maintenance work that used to sit in someone's backlog. Humans set what agents may do unsupervised and what needs review. Almost nobody is fully at stage 4, and stage 3 is where the practical gains currently sit. What agents actually do in an agentic design system Four categories, roughly in order of how commonly teams have them working: Retrieve : fetch the current token value, prop signature or usage rule for the thing being built right now Apply : generate code or designs that use the real components rather than approximations of them Detect : notice when shipped work diverges from the system and surface it Contribute : open a pull request, draft a component's documentation, propose a new token The contribution layer is where teams get nervous, reasonably. The pattern emerging from practitioners is graduated trust: agents start by suggesting only, earn the ability to make mechanical fixes, and never get autonomy over decisions that need judgement. What an agentic design system is not The term is being attached to a lot of things. Some useful exclusions: Not a chatbot over your documentation. Answering questions about the system is retrieval with a conversational wrapper. Useful, and not the same as an agent building with it. Not an MCP endpoint on its own. Exposing an endpoint says nothing about what's behind it. If it serves documentation prose, an agent still has to interpret rather than resolve. Diana Wolosin's benchmark exists precisely because plugging Markdown into MCP and calling it done is the common mistake. Not AI-generated documentation. Having an agent write your docs faster is a productivity feature for the humans maintaining the system. It doesn't change what agents can do with the output. Not full autonomy. Every practitioner working on this publicly is explicit that some decisions stay with people. An agentic system is one where the boundary is defined, not absent. How to tell which stage you're on Pick one component that gets used constantly and answer four questions about it. Question If no, you're below Can an agent get the exact token value it uses, resolved, without a person? Stage 2 Can it get the full prop signature and variant rules in structured form? Stage 2 Can it request just that component's context rather than your whole system? Stage 3 Can it propose a change to the component and route it for review? Stage 4 Most teams who run this discover they're at stage 1 with good intentions about stage 2. That's a normal place to be, and the work to move up is ordinary design system hygiene rather than anything exotic. Where the tooling fits The stages are not really a tooling question until stage 3. Naming, token architecture and component metadata are things you do to your system regardless of what platform holds it. Stage 3 is where platform matters, because serving scoped context on demand and keeping it current is infrastructure rather than authoring. It's the problem Supernova's AI context management addresses: contexts generated from the design system data itself, scoped per team or workflow, served over MCP, so an agent pulls the current value rather than a snapshot. The question worth asking your team If the credit for the ideas above belongs anywhere, it's with the practitioners publishing their work in the open. Into Design Systems has collected a substantial guide from five of them, and it's worth your time. The question to take back to your own team is narrower than "should we build an agentic design system." It's this: when one of your engineers asks an agent to build with your system tomorrow, can that agent get a specific answer, or does it have to guess? Whatever stage that puts you on is where the work starts. Supernova turns your design system into scoped, current context your agents can query — see how it works .

title: Prologis Announces Recommended Acquisition of SEGRO plc
summary: Combination expands Prologis' European platform and enhances long-term growth opportunities SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --…...
body_text: Combination expands Prologis' European platform and enhances long-term growth opportunities SAN FRANCISCO , Aug. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Prologis, Inc. (NYSE: PLD) today announced that it has reached agreement with the board of SEGRO plc (LSE: SGRO) on the terms of a recommended acquisition of SEGRO, valuing SEGRO's entire issued and to be issued ordinary share capital at approximately $18.8 billion. Daniel S. Letter, chief executive officer of Prologis, commented: "We are pleased to have reached agreement with the SEGRO Board on a combination that we believe will create meaningful value. This deal brings together SEGRO's exceptional portfolio and customer relationships with Prologis' global platform, operating expertise and financial strength. We have great respect for SEGRO, its people and the business they have built over many years. The constructive engagement between our leadership teams throughout this process has reinforced our confidence in the opportunity ahead. As we move forward, we will approach the work ahead thoughtfully and deliberately. We look forward to building on the strengths of both companies and creating even greater value for our customers and shareholders." Combination Highlights The combination will: bring together two premier portfolios in a global platform with approximately $269 billion of assets under management; strengthen the customer value proposition through a more connected global network; create a European operating portfolio of 368 million square feet, expanding Prologis' European footprint by 47%; establish a combined European development pipeline of 13 million square feet while increasing Prologis' European land bank by 126%; and expand long-term growth opportunities across logistics, energy and digital infrastructure. Transaction Terms Under the terms of the recommended acquisition, SEGRO shareholders will receive 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share. Shareholders may elect to receive cash in lieu of some or all of their Prologis share consideration, subject to the terms of the partial cash alternative. SEGRO shareholders will also be entitled to receive and retain any 2026 interim dividend of up to 10.14 pence per SEGRO share and any 2026 final dividend of up to 22.56 pence per SEGRO share, which SEGRO intends to pay prior to closing. The maximum aggregate amount of cash available under the partial cash alternative is approximately £3.5 billion. Each SEGRO shareholder's basic entitlement under the partial cash alternative is equal to 25% of the fixed price of 1,031.7 pence per SEGRO share. Accordingly, a shareholder electing to receive only its basic entitlement would receive 258 pence in cash and 0.0690 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share. Shareholders may elect to receive less than or more than their basic entitlement. Elections to receive cash in excess of the basic entitlement will be scaled back on a pro rata basis if aggregate cash elections exceed the maximum cash available. Shareholders who do not elect to participate in the partial cash alternative will receive 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share. The cash consideration payable under the partial cash alternative will be funded through a committed term loan facility, together with existing liquidity and other available sources of funding. Further details are available in the Rule 2.7 announcement, which is posted on the transaction microsite accessible through Prologis' investor relations website. Expected Financial Impact The combination is expected to enhance Prologis' long-term earnings and return potential. In the first full year following completion, assuming annualized run-rate synergies, the combination is expected to have a broadly neutral to minimally dilutive impact on Core FFO per share and AFFO per share. Prologis expects to maintain A2/A credit ratings from Moody's and S&P. Approvals and Timing The boards of Prologis and SEGRO have reached agreement on the terms of the transaction, and the SEGRO board unanimously intends to recommend it. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to the requisite approvals of SEGRO shareholders, sanction of the scheme by the court, receipt of applicable regulatory approvals and satisfaction of customary closing conditions. The transaction does not require approval by Prologis shareholders. As part of the transaction, Prologis will apply for a secondary listing of its shares on the London Stock Exchange, with the approval of that application being a condition to completion. ABOUT PROLOGIS The world runs on logistics. At Prologis, we don't just lead the industry, we define it. We create the intelligent infrastructure that powers global commerce, seamlessly connecting the digital and physical worlds. From agile supply chains to clean energy solutions, our ecosystems help your business move faster, operate smarter and grow sustainably. With unmatched scale, innovation and expertise, Prologis is a category of one–not just shaping the future of logistics but building what comes next. Learn more at Prologis.com. title: Product Bundling: Raise Your Average Order Value
summary: Bundling raises average order value because courier, COD and packing costs are per parcel. Five bundle types for Pakistani sellers and how to price them.
body_text: Bundling means selling two or more items together as one offer at one price, so a single delivery carries more value. It is the cheapest way for a small seller in Pakistan to earn more without finding a single new customer. The reason it works here is arithmetic. Your cost per order — the courier charge, the COD handling fee, the packing, the confirmation call, your time — is mostly fixed no matter what is inside the parcel. Sell one item and that cost stack eats a full margin. Sell two in the same parcel and the second item carries almost none of it. Average order value goes up, cost per order barely moves, and the difference is profit. This guide covers the bundle types that sell in Pakistan, how to price one without giving away your margin, what bundling does to your COD refusal rate, and how to run bundles when a supplier ships for you. What average order value is, and why it is the number to move Average order value is your total sales divided by your number of orders. If ten orders bring in a certain amount, the average is that amount divided by ten. Work it out for last month before you read further — most sellers have never calculated it and are surprised by how low it is. There are only three ways to grow: more customers, more orders per customer, or more value per order. The first costs money in ads. The second takes months of trust. The third you can change this afternoon by rewriting your offer. And it compounds with everything else. A higher average order value means each rupee of ad spend has more to earn back, each delivery run is worth more, and a refused parcel is a smaller share of a bigger month. Why bundles work harder under cash on delivery COD selling has costs that a prepaid model does not, and every one of them is charged per parcel rather than per item: Delivery. Couriers price by parcel and weight slab. A second small item often rides in the same slab for nothing. COD handling. Charged on the order, not the line item. Packing. One bag, one label, one strip of tape. Your time. One confirmation call, one dispatch, one follow-up — whether the parcel holds one item or four. Refusal risk. One parcel is one chance of being refused. Two separate orders are two. That last one matters more than sellers expect. Every parcel you send carries a risk of coming back, and the return leg is paid whether or not the buyer takes it. Fewer, fuller parcels is a quieter way to run the same revenue. If refusals are your main leak, work through how to reduce COD returns in Pakistan alongside this. Five bundle types that sell in Pakistan 1. The complete-the-job bundle Everything needed to finish the task the buyer came for. A phone case with a screen protector and a cleaning cloth. A hair dryer with a heat-protection spray and a round brush. A baby feeding set with the bottle brush. This is the strongest bundle type because it is not a discount, it is a favour. The buyer was going to need the second item anyway; you saved them a second search and a second delivery charge. 2. The multi-pack The same item, more than one. Socks, undergarments, kitchen cloths, storage boxes, hair ties, phone cables. Anything that gets used up, lost, or is needed by more than one person in a house. Multi-packs are the easiest bundle to launch because you do not need a second product, only a second unit — and buyers already expect a per-unit saving on quantity, so the offer explains itself. 3. The starter kit A curated set for someone doing something for the first time. A skincare starter set. A first sewing kit. A car-cleaning set. Sell the outcome, not the parts: someone buying their first set does not know what to choose, and a kit removes the choosing. 4. The variety or family pack Mixed sizes, colours or flavours in one box. It solves the buyer's biggest hesitation — picking wrong — and it lets you move slow-selling variants alongside popular ones without discounting them separately. 5. The add-on offer Not a fixed bundle. One extra item offered at the moment of ordering: "Add a spare filter for a small amount extra?" On WhatsApp this is one message after the buyer confirms, and it is the single highest-return habit in this whole guide because you are asking someone who has already decided to buy. Keep the add-on cheap relative to the main item, obviously related, and offered once. Ask twice and you sound like a call centre. Pricing a bundle without giving away the margin The discount on a bundle comes out of the second item's margin, never out of your costs. Build the price from the bottom: Add up the landed cost of every item in the bundle — what you pay the supplier, plus anything you pay to get it into the parcel. Add the per-order costs once , not once per item: courier, COD handling, packing, and a realistic allowance for refused parcels. Add your target margin on the whole bundle, in PKR rather than as a percentage. Percentages hide small numbers. Compare with the buy-separately total. Your bundle price should sit visibly below it, but the saving comes from the per-order costs you no longer pay twice — not from selling anything below its landed cost. Check the floor. If the bundle price is under the combined landed cost plus per-order costs, you are paying customers to order. Redo it. Worked example — use your own figures, never numbers copied from an article: take the supplier price of item A and item B, add them. Add your courier charge, COD fee and packing cost once. Add your margin. That is the bundle price. Now add up what those two items would cost bought separately, including two delivery charges. The gap between the two numbers is what you show the buyer. If there is no gap, the bundle is not a real offer and buyers can tell. Do this in PKR on paper before you post anything. Our breakdown of how much money you need to start dropshipping in Pakistan lays out the same cost stack for a first order. Free delivery as the bundle trigger The simplest version of bundling is a free-delivery threshold: spend above a set amount and delivery is on you. Set the threshold above your current average order value — somewhat above, not double — so it is a stretch the buyer can actually make, and make sure the margin at that threshold covers the delivery you just gave away. Choosing what to bundle Do not guess. The answer is in orders you have already taken. Read your own order history. Which two items keep appearing in the same chat? That pair is your first bundle, and it is already proven. Ask why the buyer bought. The job they hired the product for tells you what else the job needs. Bundle a fast seller with a slow one — but only where the pairing makes sense. Random pairs read as clearing old stock, because they are. Watch weight and size. A bundle that pushes into the next courier weight slab can cost more to deliver than the extra item earns. Do not bundle two fragile items. One breakage refuses the whole parcel, and you lose both margins plus the return leg. Keep it to two or three items. Longer bundles are harder to photograph, harder to price and harder to restock. If you are still building the catalogue, browse by product category — bundles are easiest to assemble inside one category, where the items ship together and suit the same buyer. Our list of the best home and kitchen products to resell in Pakistan is a good hunting ground, because kitchen items bundle naturally into sets. If you are still setting up the supplier and courier side in your city, our Lahore supplier and COD guide covers that half, and the same slabs-and-suppliers logic applies wherever you are based. Presenting the bundle so it actually sells A bundle that is not obvious is not a bundle. Four things do most of the work: One photo with everything laid out. All items visible in one frame, on a plain background. Buyers must see what they get without reading. A name, not a list. "Kitchen Starter Set" beats "chopper + peeler + grater". Name the outcome. One price, with the saving stated once. Show the bundle price and what the items cost separately. Say it plainly and move on. A description that covers every item. Sizes, materials, what is in the box — for each piece. Vague bundle listings cause the "this is not what I expected" refusal at the door. Our guide to writing product descriptions that sell has a structure you can reuse per item. Then say it out loud in the places buyers actually see you: pin the bundle to the top of your WhatsApp catalogue, put it in the first line of your bio, and film it once. A packing clip showing everything going into the bag works well if you are reselling on TikTok in Pakistan , because the value is visible in five seconds. Bundling when the supplier ships for you Dropshippers can bundle, with one rule: check how the items dispatch before you sell them as one offer. On Markaz you order per item with no minimum, the supplier ships, and cash on delivery is collected and settled to you in PKR. Two items from the same supplier usually travel together. Two items from different suppliers may arrive on different days, and a buyer who paid one price for one bundle will not accept half of it at the door. So, three checks before you list a bundle you do not pack yourself: Same supplier where possible. One dispatch, one parcel, one cash collection. Same delivery window. Local stock runs 3–5 days; items coming from China run roughly 10–17 days. Bundling one of each means the buyer waits for the slower one — say so up front, or do not pair them. Same cash amount at the door. The rider collects one figure. Make sure it matches the figure you quoted, for the whole bundle. Where the delivery windows do not line up, sell the bundle as a pre-order with the honest date, or build it entirely from China deals so the whole set arrives on the same timeline. Track the dispatches in the dropshipping portal rather than in a chat thread — a split bundle is the order you most need to be able to look up. What bundling does to your refusal rate Higher order value means more cash at the door, and more cash at the door means a slightly higher chance the buyer changes their mind. Bundles pay for themselves anyway, but do not pretend the effect is zero. Three things keep it small: Confirm the total before dispatch. One message stating the items, the bundle price and the delivery window. Never let the amount be a surprise. Show the saving in the confirmation. Reminding the buyer what they saved is the cheapest way to keep an order warm. Do not bundle upward too fast. Doubling your average order value in one step raises refusals more than a steady climb. Move the number, then hold it. The whole order-to-cash flow, including where refusals come from, is covered in COD dropshipping in Pakistan . Mistakes that make bundles lose money Discounting from the retail price instead of building from cost. The saving must come from the per-order costs you avoid, not from your margin. Bundling items nobody buys together. A pairing that makes no sense reads as stock clearance and gets ignored. Ignoring the weight slab. Check the courier's slabs before you set the price, not after the first month's bill. Too many items. Three is plenty. More is a photograph nobody can read. Running every product as a bundle. Keep single units available. Some buyers only want the one thing, and a forced bundle loses that sale entirely. Never measuring. If you do not know your average order value before and after, you have no idea whether the bundle worked. A two-week test Day 1. Work out last month's average order value. Write the number down. Day 2. Read your order history and find the two items that keep appearing together. Day 3. Price that pair from cost upward, and check it against the buy-separately total. Day 4. Shoot one flat-lay photo of the bundle and name it after the outcome. Day 5. Pin it to your catalogue and post it once. Days 6–13. Offer the add-on to every buyer who confirms an order. One message, once. Day 14. Recalculate the average order value. Compare it with day 1, and check your refusal rate moved with it. If the number went up and refusals held steady, build the second bundle. If refusals climbed, the bundle price outran what your buyers are ready to hand over at the door — bring it down a step and try again. Starting from scratch, how to start a reselling business in Pakistan covers the groundwork before this, and the Markaz reseller guide has the model in one place. Start with the pair you already sell You do not need new products or an ad budget to raise your average order value. You need one honest pairing, priced from cost upward, photographed once, and offered to every buyer who was already going to order. Measure the number before you start and again two weeks later. That comparison is the only proof that matters.

title: Introducing a New Label for AI-Generated Artist Identities on Spotify
summary: True artist-fan connection can only be built on a foundation of trust and authenticity. In music, that means listeners need to be able to trust that the artist behind the music is who they say they are. That’s more essential than ever in the age of generative AI. So this year, we’ve made Artist Identity...
body_text: True artist-fan connection can only be built on a foundation of trust and authenticity. In music, that means listeners need to be able to trust that the artist behind the music is who they say they are. That’s more essential than ever in the age of generative AI. So this year, we’ve made Artist Identity & Trust one of our very top priorities with the launch of Verified by Spotify, SongDNA, AI Credits, and Artist Profile Protection. Today, we’re announcing another step in our effort to ensure Spotify is the most transparent and trustworthy place to listen to music. Listeners have been clear in telling us that they don’t like seeing an artist profile that seems human, only to find out that the persona is AI-generated. That’s why, starting mid-September, you’ll begin to see an AI Persona badge on some artist profiles. The badge signals to listeners that an artist’s identity may be AI-generated and does not represent a real person. Alongside artist profiles that self-disclose as AI Personas, we will also start applying badges to relevant profiles. By default, Spotify will not include AI Personas in any editorial or algorithmic recommendations. That means you won’t see any music from AI Personas in your personalized recommendations, unless you follow AI Personas, for example. While we believe all artists have creative choice in determining how they present themselves, Spotify’s programming is focused on elevating music from authentic artists building careers in music. How it works Starting today, artists can share that their profile represents an AI Persona through Spotify for Artists. We hope artists will be transparent, so we are giving them the opportunity to disclose, but we won’t rely on self-disclosure alone. Spotify will also review artist profiles and identify those whose public identity—the identity an artist presents on their profile, including name and imagery—appears to represent photorealistic AI-generated identities. We’ll start with artists who have met defined audience thresholds, so the labels cover the vast majority of artist profiles that users visit. In mid-September, you’ll start to see the AI Persona badge appear on artist profiles (in the banner and About section), in Search, and on track rows across playlists. When listeners tap the badge, they’ll be able to see whether the artist transparently shared that they’re an AI Persona to build trust with potential listeners, or if Spotify had to review and make an informed determination. For artist profiles where Spotify’s review team have applied the badge, artists will be notified and given the opportunity to self-disclose or appeal. In the coming months, we’ll also give listeners the ability to report artist profiles they believe represent AI Personas to our review team. We’ll share more details when that’s available. Although there’s a broad spectrum in how artists use AI as a creative tool, the question of whether a profile represents an actual human is one where Spotify can help make a clear determination. This badge is about the artist’s public identity, not about how the music was made. For more information about how the music was made, we offer AI Credits and SongDNA . With AI credits, we have seen that people are eager to take the opportunity to be transparent and share how they used AI as part of their song’s creative process. We’re hoping for a similar level of self disclosure for AI Personas. Building trust and transparency on Spotify AI Persona badges are part of our broader efforts to make Spotify the most transparent and trustworthy place to listen to music. In 2026, we’ve introduced several other features designed to give listeners more transparency about what they’re hearing and who’s behind it. Verified by Spotify signals to listeners an artist is a real human presenting themselves authentically on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of profiles are already verified, the majority of which are independent artists, representing more than 99% of the artists Spotify listeners actively search. AI Credits allow artists to disclose to listeners how they used AI in their music creation, with tens of thousands of AI credits submitted daily. SongDNA gives listeners deeper context on the artists and contributors behind a track, helping them discover and fall in love with the human creative process. Artist Details surfaces artist information based on Spotify’s own platform data, such as career milestones, release history, and touring activity, giving listeners a quick snapshot of an artist’s authentic activity on Spotify. Artist Profile Protection lets artists review and approve releases delivered to Spotify to protect their artist identity and prevent listener confusion about misattributed music. In addition to these features, we tune our algorithms to highlight authentic human artists and, based on available signals, strive to not include spam, slop, or low-effort content in our recommendations. We know the music ecosystem is evolving, and so will our approach. We’ll continue to adapt as the landscape changes and as we learn from artists, listeners, and industry partners.

title: The best Saleshandy alternatives in 2026
summary: Saleshandy alternatives for 2026, ranked. Artisan writes, sends, and answers cold email for you, plus Instantly, Woodpecker, QuickMail and more.
body_text: The best Saleshandy alternative for most teams is Artisan, because it does the part Saleshandy leaves to you: Ava, Artisan's AI business development representative (BDR), writes the cold email, sends it with managed deliverability, and answers the replies autonomously. Saleshandy is a fine budget starting rung. If you have outgrown it, the answer is not another sender. Saleshandy earns its place as a low-cost entry point: it bundles a lead finder with sending and sequencing so a new team can prospect and send from one tool without stitching sources together. That is a useful first rung. But teams outgrow starter senders in two directions. Some need heavier deliverability infrastructure as volume climbs. Others realize the cheap software still leaves all the writing and replying to a human, and they want that work automated. This guide ranks both paths honestly. Saleshandy alternatives compared Rank Tool Best for Standout capability Public pricing 1 Artisan Teams that want cold email written, sent, and answered for them Ava, an autonomous AI BDR with managed deliverability Usage-based credits, no platform fee, free trial 2 Instantly High-volume senders that want deliverability infrastructure Mailbox rotation at scale, large lead database $47-555/mo 3 Woodpecker Small teams that want usage-based sending Pay-per-prospect pricing, unlimited inboxes About $7 per 100 prospects contacted 4 QuickMail Teams that want proven inbox rotation Inbox rotation heritage, deliverability focus Published per-tier pricing 5 Smartlead Agencies that run many client inboxes Unlimited mailbox rotation, deep API $39-379/mo (placement testing extra) 6 Lemlist Personalization-first multichannel sequences Custom images and variables in outreach $69-109/user/mo (annual) How we chose Four criteria, weighted for a buyer who has outgrown a starter sender: 1. How much of the job the tool does. A bundled lead finder plus sending is a start. The differentiator is whether the tool also writes and replies. 2. Deliverability at scale. Inbox placement testing, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks, sender reputation monitoring, dynamic send limits, and automatic pausing of unhealthy mailboxes. 3. Pricing transparency. Published tiers beat quote-on-request, and we flag add-ons that inflate the real cost. 4. Deployment fit. Whether one operator can run it, or whether it needs a dedicated cold email specialist. Why do teams look for a Saleshandy alternative? Most switch because Saleshandy is a starter tool, and starter tools have a ceiling by design. The low price and bundled lead finder make it easy to launch a first motion, but the model assumes a person does the actual selling work: writing every message, choosing every target, and answering every reply. As a team's volume and personalization needs rise, the cheap software becomes the thing capping them. The triggers we hear most: Growth outpaces the tool. A bundled lead finder is convenient early, but its data depth and deliverability tooling have poorer coverage than a dedicated stack, and volume exposes that. The manual load never shrinks. Saleshandy sends what you write. The human hours spent writing and replying are exactly the same at 10,000 emails as at 1,000. Personalization stays basic. Starter senders lean on light token-swapping, so as reply rates fall industry-wide, teams want truly per-recipient messaging the tool cannot generate. None of this makes Saleshandy a bad first rung. It makes it the wrong long-term home for a team that wants outbound to scale without scaling the manual work. For fundamentals, see our guide to cold emailing . The best Saleshandy alternatives in 2026 1. Artisan: The AI BDR that writes, sends, and replies Artisan is the alternative for teams that want the outbound job owned, not just cheaply enabled. Instead of a starter sender you feed, Artisan gives you Ava, an autonomous AI BDR. Ava finds best-fit leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals across over 200 countries, plus Artisan Local Data covering over 250 million local businesses, enriches and ranks them by likelihood of converting, writes personalized cold email where two people in the same campaign receive two different messages, sends it with managed deliverability, and handles the replies: qualifying, answering objections from your knowledge base, chasing follow-ups, and booking meetings on your reps' calendars. Where Saleshandy bundles a light lead finder, Artisan runs deep sourcing and enrichment with natural-language search, ideal customer profile (ICP) filters, and intent signals such as funding rounds, new executive hires, and active hiring. Where Saleshandy stops at basic sending, Artisan manages the whole deliverability stack: mailbox provisioning and management, inbox placement testing, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks, dynamic send limits, inbox rotation, health monitoring, and auto-pausing of unhealthy mailboxes. Control is adjustable rather than binary: review and approve every message, restrict Ava to objection-handling only, or let her run fully autonomous with plain-language escalation rules and a full audit trail. Artisan reports over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously. The economics fit a growing team. Pricing is usage-based, so you pay for the work Ava performs rather than per seat, and there is a free trial. For larger teams, sales ops can run Ava centrally for an account executive (AE) team whose reps never log in, with cross-channel do-not-contact enforcement and CRM owner routing. Artisan is SOC 2 Type II compliant, GDPR and CCPA compliant, with SSO and role-based access on Enterprise plans. "We've sourced over $700k of ARR in the past 6 months, which is 20x our investment in Artisan. The ROI is undeniable," said Henri Delahaye, Founder of Chain of Events, whose team replaced the workload of five human BDRs while one person spends four to five hours a week managing every campaign. See Artisan pricing for the current model. Best for: startups through enterprise that want cold email written, sent, and answered autonomously, with deliverability and sourcing managed for them. Who should pick something else: brand-new teams that only want the cheapest possible way to test a first outbound motion by hand. Pricing: usage-based credits, no platform fee, free trial. See artisan.co/pricing . 2. Instantly: Volume sending infrastructure Instantly is the alternative for teams whose next constraint is sending capacity. It built the category's biggest sending engine: mailbox rotation at scale, deliverability infrastructure, and a large lead database. For a team graduating from a starter sender because volume is climbing, Instantly is the natural infrastructure upgrade. The trade is that Instantly is infrastructure-first, so copywriting, targeting, and reply-handling stay yours, and reviewers report its AI features arrived later than the sending tooling. Public tiers run $47 to $555 per month, per its pricing page, scaling with mailboxes, lead credits, and seats. For comparisons, see Apollo vs. Instantly and Artisan vs. Instantly . Best for: high-volume senders that want reliable deliverability infrastructure they operate themselves. Who should pick something else: teams that want the copy and replies handled instead of the sending enabled. Pricing: $47-555/mo, per Instantly's pricing page. 3. Woodpecker: Simple usage-based sending Woodpecker is the closest spiritual sibling to Saleshandy for a small team: predictable pricing, unlimited inboxes, and a clean interface. It charges roughly $7 per 100 prospects contacted, which suits spiky or seasonal volume better than a subscription. Deliverability tooling is solid for its class. Woodpecker is deliberately narrow, lighter on multichannel and AI. It does not bundle a lead finder the way Saleshandy does, so you supply the list, but the usage pricing and inbox limits are friendlier as you grow. For a small team that mostly wants reliable, affordable email, this focus is a feature. For a multichannel option, see the best La Growth Machine alternatives . Best for: small teams that want usage pricing and unlimited inboxes. Who should pick something else: teams that need bundled sourcing, heavy infrastructure, or the work done for them. Pricing: usage-based, roughly $7 per 100 prospects contacted, per Woodpecker's pricing page. 4. QuickMail: Proven inbox rotation QuickMail is the pick for a team upgrading from a starter sender specifically because deliverability matters more as volume climbs. It pioneered inbox rotation, spreading sends across mailboxes to protect sender reputation, and this discipline anchors the product. Where Saleshandy's deliverability is basic, QuickMail's is a genuine strength. QuickMail is narrower than a full suite, lighter on multichannel, and, as with the rest of this tier, it sends what you write and leaves the replies for you to handle. QuickMail publishes per-tier pricing on its site. Best for: teams that want deliverability discipline as they scale volume. Who should pick something else: teams that want the writing and replies handled. Pricing: published per-tier pricing, per QuickMail's pricing page. 5. Smartlead: The agency and API workhorse Smartlead is the pick for teams whose growth takes them toward an agency or multi-client model. Unlimited mailbox rotation, a deep API, and a master inbox for many accounts make it built for running dozens of sending domains at once, well beyond a starter sender's scope. For agency-focused options, see the best outbound tools for agencies . The cost math needs a note: core tiers run $39 to $379 per month, but placement testing is billed separately at $49 to $599, so the effective price climbs once you turn on serious-sender features. And like Saleshandy, Smartlead is infrastructure. You still write and reply. Best for: agencies and API-first teams that run many inboxes across clients. Who should pick something else: teams that want the work handled or dislike add-on surprises. Pricing: $39-379/mo core; placement testing $49-599 extra, per Smartlead's pricing page. 6. Lemlist: Personalization-first multichannel Lemlist is the alternative for teams that outgrow a starter sender because their messaging needs to stand out. It pioneered custom images and dynamic variables inside cold email and runs multichannel sequences. Bootstrapped to roughly $40M in revenue and having acquired the video tool Claap in October 2025, it is a serious independent company. The trade is that Lemlist's personalization is powerful but manual: you build the tokens, images, and logic. It scales creativity, not headcount. Pricing runs $69 to $109/user/month on annual billing, per its pricing page. For comparisons, see Apollo vs. Lemlist and Artisan vs. Lemlist . Best for: teams that want visually personalized multichannel sequences and will build them by hand. Who should pick something else: teams that want personalization generated for them at scale. Pricing: $69-109/user/mo on annual billing, per Lemlist's pricing page. Stay with Saleshandy if... Saleshandy is the right call for a specific profile. Keep it if: You are launching a first outbound motion and want the cheapest way to prospect and send from one tool. Your volume is modest and a bundled lead finder covers your list-building needs. Your team writes and replies happily, so the manual model is a fit rather than a burden. Switching tools to solve a writing-and-reply problem that Saleshandy was never meant to solve is a mistake. If the manual load is the bottleneck, that is the signal to move to an autonomous AI BDR instead. Frequently asked questions What is the best alternative to Saleshandy? For teams that want cold email written, sent, and answered for them, Artisan is the strongest alternative, because Ava runs the full outbound job autonomously with managed deliverability and sourcing. For a like-for-like budget sender with friendlier usage pricing, Woodpecker is the closest direct rival. What is the best enterprise alternative to Saleshandy? Artisan. Saleshandy is a starter tool with no real enterprise story, so the upgrade adds central sales-ops deployment for large AE teams, cross-channel do-not-contact governance, CRM owner routing, an audit trail, and SOC 2 Type II compliance, all of which a budget sender lacks. Is Woodpecker better than Saleshandy? For a small team, often it is a close call: both are affordable senders. Woodpecker's usage pricing (roughly $7 per 100 prospects contacted) and unlimited inboxes scale more gracefully, while Saleshandy bundles a lead finder Woodpecker does not. Neither writes or replies for you. How much does Saleshandy cost? Saleshandy publishes low per-tier pricing on its site, from $25 to $209 per month on annual billing, which is its main appeal as an entry point. The trade for this low price is limited information, deliverability, and personalization compared with a dedicated stack, and no autonomous writing or reply-handling. Can I replace Saleshandy with an AI SDR? Yes, and it is often the reason teams leave. An autonomous AI sales agent like Ava sources leads, writes personalized email, manages deliverability, and answers replies, covering Saleshandy's function plus the manual work that a starter sender leaves entirely to you. Which Saleshandy alternative is cheapest? Woodpecker's usage model and Saleshandy's own tiers are among the cheapest per message. But cheapest per message is not cheapest per meeting booked, which is where autonomous tools change the math. Compare the full field in the best cold email tools . See also the best cold email marketing software and best email outbound tools .

title: Exploratory data analysis of a drug-biomarker-efficacy PD model
summary: Explore how PK/PD modeling of paired biomarker and efficacy data yields initial parameter estimates and a new mechanistic in vivo potency expression.
body_text: Share Share Share Date: Wednesday, August 19, 2026 Time: 10:00 - 11:00 am ET Discovery Early Clinical Preclinical Products: Phoenix® , R Speaks NLME (RsNLME) , Pirana® PMX Modeling Software Certara University Register here Summary This webinar walks through a real-world exploratory analysis of a PK/PD model where a drug inhibits a biomarker (its primary target), and that biomarker in turn inhibits clinical efficacy — two sequential inhibitory steps that together drive efficacy back toward baseline. You’ll see how initial parameter estimates are derived from biomarker and efficacy time-course data, and how a new in vivo potency expression captures the underlying target-binding and turnover dynamics more completely than a single potency parameter. Key learning objectives: How to derive initial parameter estimates from paired biomarker and efficacy time-course data for a sequential-inhibition PD model. How drug-target binding (kon/koff), target turnover (R0, kdeg), and complex elimination (ke(RC)) combine into a new expression for in vivo potency. How to replace a single potency parameter with a mechanistic expression that better reflects target engagement. How equilibrium expressions describe target inhibition and efficacy build-up as functions of drug concentration. Why this generic double-inhibition framework applies broadly to any system with two sequential negative (inhibitory) actions. This webinar is ideal for: Any PK/PD scientists including Phoenix, Pirana, RsNLME users. Speakers: Johan Gabrielsson Bernd Wendt, PhD Senior Director of Customer Success Bernd has been teaching as a trainer at Certara and is a lecturer at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (Munich) for more than 5 years, providing seminars in pharmacokinetics and molecular modeling. He is currently heading the global support group at Certara. body_text: Best Free SAT Prep in 2026: 9 Tools That Actually Work TL;DR The best free SAT prep in 2026 is not a single app. It is a combination of tools: Miyagi Labs for a guided diagnostic and study path, College Board Bluebook for official full-length practice tests, Khan Academy for free lessons, the College Board Student Question Bank for targeted drilling, and Desmos practice for Math speed. Most students only need three or four of these to see real improvement, and the biggest gains come from reviewing mistakes, not collecting resources. Quick Takeaway If you only remember one thing from this guide, remember this: The highest-scoring students usually do not use the most SAT resources—they use the right resources consistently. A simple study plan using one official practice test, one lesson platform, one official question bank, and careful mistake review is often more effective than jumping between dozens of apps. For most students, the best free SAT prep stack is: Need Best Resource Practice tests Bluebook Lessons Khan Academy Official practice questions Student Question Bank Personalized study plan Miyagi Labs Math calculator skills Desmos This combination covers nearly every part of the Digital SAT without spending money. Which Free SAT Resource Should You Start With? If you are completely new to SAT preparation, follow this order. Take one Bluebook diagnostic test. Identify your weakest skills. Learn those concepts using Khan Academy. Practice with the Student Question Bank. Repeat another official test after two to three weeks. Students who already know their weaknesses can skip directly to targeted practice instead of starting from scratch. Direct Answer The best free SAT prep in 2026 is a combination of official College Board resources and one platform that organizes your studying. Why Free SAT Prep Is Better Than You Think More than 2 million students in the class of 2025 took the SAT. At $68 per registration, that is a lot of money before a student even buys a single prep book. The good news: the best free SAT prep tools available right now are strong enough to build a complete study plan, if you know what to use and when. The SAT is now fully digital. It uses two adaptive sections (Reading and Writing, and Math), short passages instead of long ones, and an embedded Desmos calculator for the entire Math section. Any prep resource that still assumes the old paper format is wasting your time. The problem is not a shortage of free resources. It is fragmentation. How We Ranked Free SAT Prep Resources Every resource on this list was evaluated on six criteria: Digital SAT fit. Resources that offer Bluebook-like tools (timer, Desmos calculator, mark-for-review, option eliminator) scored higher on test-day realism. Official SAT Resources vs Third-Party Resources Students often ask whether they should only use official College Board resources. The answer is no. Both official and third-party resources serve different purposes. Official Resources Third-Party Resources Most accurate question style More practice questions Real SAT interface Better explanations Limited number of tests Unlimited practice Best score calibration Better analytics Highest realism More personalization The strongest study plans combine both rather than relying exclusively on one category. What Makes a Free SAT Resource Actually Good? Not every free SAT website is worth your time. The best resources share several characteristics. Updated for the Digital SAT The SAT changed significantly when it became fully digital. Good resources should include: adaptive modules shorter reading passages Desmos calculator support current SAT question styles Avoid resources that still focus on the old paper SAT. Uses Official or High-Quality Questions Official College Board questions are the closest representation of the real exam. Third-party resources can still be excellent, but question quality varies considerably. Teaches Concepts Instead of Memorization Good prep explains: why an answer is correct why wrong answers are tempting how to avoid repeating mistakes Helps You Build a Study Plan Random practice is rarely effective.
